findings.title: Incomplete or contradictory positive references can unlock boot and interventions

evidence.facts: read_reference requires identity/counts/verdict but does not require the emitted pf-witness-oracle record, validate the complete schema fields or their cross-record relationships. Original pairing checks attempts only (plus altered and frames); intervention pairing checks selected accepted counts, altered/oracle_mismatches and one selected first row. The consume check accepts any single pattern where fact==expected, without validating host/raw-word/change consistency.

Current positive-first damaged-reference controls exercise mode/setup/pairing/some counts/fault rows, but not missing oracle, contradictory attempt/answered/accepted/oracle counts or incoherent consumption tuples.

findings.concrete_failure: Starting from a valid Original report, remove its oracle row or change answered_set/accepted_set to a nonzero whole count while attempts_set stays0 and the PASS verdict stays unchanged: flags_control still accepts it before boot. Starting from a valid paired control, remove the oracle row or contradict answered/attempt counts while retaining accepted_group/set/reset>0, the selected first row and PASS: a refusal mode still proceeds. For read_changed, an edited consume tuple fact=expected=0x00000000 passes the precondition although UPDATED must be1.0 or2.0, and its other tuple fields are not required. These are source-derived counterexamples, not executed probes.
findings.impact: The claimed whole successful same-setup positive is not actually established before effects. A damaged positive packet can authorize a native intervention and its refusal credit.
minimum_correction: Validate the complete schema1 reference records required by each role, their multiplicities/order and canonical field domains before output creation/preparation/boot. A healthy reference requires no fatal/request/reply fault, no intervention, no backing mismatch and coherent attempt/answered/accepted/key/oracle relationships; Original must have zero flag traffic throughout, not just zero attempts.

Join oracle record values to counts, first-event records to count/frame/ordinal bounds and the event actually eligible, and any consume tuple to complete legal UPDATED1.0/2.0/raw-word/change relationships. Preserve the legitimate group/set/reset-only control with no consumable read: it may support only cases its actual positive reached.

Use a real generated successful Original and paired control first; damage one field/required row at a time (including missing oracle, accepted>attempted, inconsistent oracle, impossible first prefix and incoherent/missing consumption fields). Each must reject for that field before report creation, boot, provider calls or alteration; retain genuine parent RED and corrected GREEN. No native damaged-reference run or new production API is needed.

findings.title: A delayed unrelated fatal at the same marker can receive refusal credit

evidence.facts: An injected refusal sets intervened1, but creates no pending immediate-refusal latch. Subsequent callbacks run normally. decide credits intervened1 plus a later fatal whose marker matches, without checking continuation after the bad answer.
Current tests prove direct refusal and fatal-before-intervention rejection, but do not cover an engine ignoring the injected fault, continuing through another callback, then raising the same marker.

findings.concrete_failure: A scripted campaign can receive/ignore the injected malformed or wrong reply, call another host callback, and then raise the configured marker later in that frame. No request/reply fault need be recorded by the witness, altered remains1 and decide reaches PASS at629. The fatal did not demonstrate immediate rejection of the altered answer. This is a source-derived counterexample; no experiment was replayed.
findings.impact: The single-fault causal boundary proof can falsely pass an accepted bad reply followed by an unrelated failure.
minimum_correction: Latch the refusal transaction when the eligible fault is injected. Any subsequent host callback or normal return from that engine entry before its fatal must invalidate refusal credit, even if a later fatal has the same marker. Keep real malformed positive/reply/oracle faults and unrelated fatal failures ahead of UNREACHED.

Bind expected fatal capture to the actual engine entry/phase. frame calls are guarded today; boot is only inside the outer xpcall and does not populate fatal. Where the declared first eligible event can occur during boot, capture that actual entry consistently without any getter/counter/close through a poisoned engine; do not manufacture a fatal or silently credit another phase.

Retain a successful paired positive, direct genuine refusal per mode, and clean UNREACHED. Add positive-first controls that ignore the fault then (a) continue a callback and raise the same marker, (b) return normally, or (c) raise a different marker; all must fail. Preserve fatal-before-intervention failures and the valid changed-answer path; no C/Rust product change or native bad-input run is required.
